newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Kaifa plans US$40 mln venture with IBM.
newsitem.headline: Kaifa plans US$40 mln venture with IBM.

text.p: Shenzhen Kaifa Technology Co Ltd said on Wednesday it was planning a second computer-parts venture in Shenzhen with International Business Machines Corp.
The project has been approved by China's State Planning Commission, a company official told the China Securities Bulletin.
The official said IBM would have a 75 percent stake in the venture, Shenzhen Hailiang Storage Product Co Ltd, which requires US$40 million in total investment.
Kaifa would hold 10 percent and China Great Wall Computer Group Co 15 percent.
The venture should be operational later this year, the official said. He gave no other details.
Kaifa is already already involved in a computer parts venture in Shenzhen with IBM and Great Wall.
In its 1995 annual report Kaifa said it had taken a 15 percent stake in Shenzhen Changke International Electronic Co Ltd in the second half of 1995 by contributing US$1.35 million.
IBM held 60 percent of Changke and Great Wall 25 percent.
More than 90 percent of Kaifa's products, including disk drives and floppy disks, are exported, the official said.
